newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia's productivity seen growing 6 pct in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia's productivity seen growing 6 pct in 1997.

text.p: Malaysia's national productivity is expected to grow six percent in 1997 after 5.7 percent growth last year, National Productivity Corp (NPC) said in its 1996 Productivity Report released on Thursday.
The slower growth in 1996 after a 6.6 percent expansion in 1995 was due to a drop in the growth of the construction and electricity sectors and a slowdown in external demand, it said.

The major factor in productivity growth in 1996 continued to be the manufacturing sector which contributed 48.0 percent, followed by the aggregate services sector comprising commerce/trade (15.2 percent), finance (13.2 percent) and transport (13.0 percent).
Productivity in the manufacturing sector was expected to grow 6.2 percent this year after a 5.8 percent expansion in 1996, NPC said.
Employment in the sector was projected to rise 6.9 percent, while manufacturing output was expected to increase 13.5 percent, it added.
"Given these conditions, the manufacturing sector will contribute 34.6 percent to gross domestic product and provide 27.5 percent of total employment in the economy," NPC said.
Malaysia's GDP is officially forecast to grow eight percent in 1997 after 8.5 percent growth last year.
Productivity in commerce/trade was expected to grow 6.8 percent, transport 6.7 percent and finance six percent this year, NPC said.
Overall employment growth in 1997 was expected to be maintained at last year's 2.8 percent after three percent growth in 1995, it added.
